study_id: Sage et al. - 2023 - A machine-learning approach to human ex vivo lung perfusion predicts transplantation outcomes and pr

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study involves adult lung transplant candidates, uses a non‑linear machine‑learning model (XGBoost) to predict post‑transplant outcomes, compares against standard clinical practice, and is a peer‑reviewed article published in 2023.

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective study using ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) data from 2008 to 2022 to develop and validate an AI model for transplant outcome prediction.
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Clinical EVLP cases from Toronto General Hospital (UHN) database
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included consecutive clinical EVLP cases from 2008‑2022; adult donors and recipients with end‑stage lung disease.
identification_methods.Comparator: Standard EVLP assessment without AI assistance
identification_methods.Input Variables: Donor demographics, donor type, physiological (compliance, gas exchange), biochemical (glucose, lactate, pH, base excess), imaging, cytokine levels (IL‑6, IL‑8, IL‑10, IL‑1β), and EVLP circuit parameters.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Missing values handled by XGBoost algorithm and supplemented from original source documents.
identification_methods.Validation Method: Five‑fold cross‑validation on development set and temporal validation using two independent test datasets (2019‑2020, 2020‑2022).
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Developed using class‑weighted XGBoost with 5‑fold CV; separate temporal validation cohorts; recipient model added via random forest; performance assessed with AUROC and AUPRC.

population.Inclusion criteria: Adults with end-stage lung disease referred for first lung transplantation
population.Exclusion criteria: Double lung EVLP assessments that resulted in single lung transplantation
population.Population Notes: Data split into development cohort (n=504) and two validation cohorts (n=97, n=124); total EVLP cases from 2008-2022
population.Ischemic Time: Median warm ischemic time 65 min [IQR: 50–80 min]
population.Ischemic Time Overall: Median warm ischemic time 65 min [IQR: 50–80 min]

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Donor clinical data and EVLP assessments (physiological, biochemical, imaging, biological measurements) collected longitudinally
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: Model-inherent feature importance via SHAP; no separate selection method reported
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Longitudinal features extracted up to four hours of EVLP (min, max, trend, last value)
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: InsighTx model trained on 725 EVLP cases using donor and EVLP features; recipient features added in secondary modeling
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Extubation <72 h post‑transplant, Extubation ≥72 h post‑transplant, Unsuitable for transplantation
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcomes are classification of post‑transplant ventilation duration and transplant suitability
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Performance reported as AUROC with standard deviations for training and two independent test datasets
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All EVLP cases evaluated for post‑transplant ventilation outcome
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUROC calculated on held‑out test cohorts for predicting extubation <72 h
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: High discrimination for suitable lungs; AUROC varies across datasets
